hero.title: Membership
hero.intro: Membership is personal, closed, and held by invitation and consideration. What follows sets out who it suits and how it is entered.

whoShouldJoin.title: Who should join
whoShouldJoin.intro: The Circle is deliberately narrow. It suits a particular kind of leader more than a particular kind of company.

criteria.title: Leading an established organisation
criteria.body: Membership is held by those carrying final responsibility, rather than by those advising on it.

criteria.title: Long past needing an audience
criteria.body: The Circle suits leaders who have nothing left to prove in public and a great deal still to work out in private.

criteria.title: Prepared to contribute
criteria.body: Members are expected to give counsel as readily as they take it. A quiet year is fine; a passive one is not.

criteria.title: Discreet by disposition
criteria.body: Everything within the Circle depends on confidence being kept without being asked for.

categories.title: Membership Categories
categories.intro: Membership is held in one of three categories. Each carries a different depth of involvement; all three are entered the same way.

items.name: Executive Circle
items.body: For leaders taking their place among peers. Full access to the forums, the briefings and the network, with counsel available as questions arise rather than on a schedule.

photo.alt: Business, man and thinking at city on rooftop about career or future with goal in company. Professional, person and skyscraper on roof is standing with vision or hope for decision as leader at work.
photo.note: Documentary: a working session or boardroom, mid-conversation.

items.name: Elite Circle
items.body: For members who shape the Circle's agenda as well as draw on it. Adds a standing advisory group and a council seat, and a hand in setting what the year's programme takes on.

photo.alt: Handsome businessman with smartphone on sofa indoors. Luxury lifestyle
photo.note: Documentary: a small group in discussion, candid rather than posed.

items.name: Chairman's Circle
items.body: Entered by invitation from the chair. Convenes the smallest rooms in the Circle, holds its governance, and carries a say in who is invited to join next.

photo.alt: Middle eastern and caucasian businessmen shaking hands outdoor on a sunny day
photo.note: Documentary: a formal room or a single figure, quiet and composed.

benefits.title: Membership Benefits
benefits.intro: What membership provides, stated plainly. Nothing here depends on volume — the Circle is built to be small.

features.label: Counsel
features.body: Access to peers who have faced comparable decisions, in settings built for candour rather than display.

features.label: Introductions
features.body: Considered introductions made by the Circle, in both directions, and only where both parties stand to gain.

features.label: Standing
features.body: A place within a membership that is closed, and whose value rests on remaining so.

features.label: Reach
features.body: Councils and delegations that extend a member's context beyond their own market.

journey.title: Membership Journey
journey.intro: From first conversation to invitation. The sequence is short, and deliberately unhurried.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.body: Most members arrive through another member. Where they do not, the first conversation establishes whether the Circle is the right room.

steps.title: Conversation
steps.body: An unhurried discussion about what you are working on and what you would want from the membership.

steps.title: Consideration
steps.body: Your candidacy is considered within the Circle. The question is fit rather than qualification.

steps.title: Invitation
steps.body: Where consideration is favourable, an invitation follows, along with the terms of membership.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.intro: The questions we are asked most often, answered as directly as we can before a conversation begins.

items.title: Can I apply directly?
items.body: Yes. Most members are introduced by an existing member, but a direct request is considered on the same footing.

items.title: What is expected of a member?
items.body: Presence and candour more than time. Members are asked to attend what they commit to, and to give counsel as readily as they take it.

items.title: Is the membership list published?
items.body: Confidentiality terms — including how members are identified — are set out in the Trust Framework, which is being finalised. We would rather point you there than summarise it here.

items.title: How long does consideration take?
items.body: It varies with the enquiry. The Circle would rather take the time to get the fit right than move to a schedule.

items.title: Can membership be held by a company?
items.body: No. Membership is personal to the individual and does not transfer with a role.
